chain.label: Federal flight/duty time rules ignore fatigue factors
chain.trigger: these regulations do not take into consideration the starting time of day, the length of the duty day, the number of flight segments, weather conditions... or other factors that might affect a pilot's workload, and thus, a pilot's fatigue

chain.label: Both pilots fatigued after a long duty day begun with an early wakeup
chain.trigger: it had been more than 15 hours since the pilots' last significant sleep period, and they had been on duty for 14 1/2 hours

caused_by.evidence: existing FAA pilot duty regulations do not reflect recent research on pilot fatigue and sleep issues, increasing the possibility that pilots will fly in a fatigued condition

chain.label: Night approach over unlit terrain with almost no ground references
chain.trigger: there were minimal lights or ground references beneath the approach course that would have helped the pilots judge the airplane's position relative to the runway or height above terrain

chain.label: Night IMC at destination: 300-foot overcast, 3 to 4 miles in mist
chain.trigger: ceiling overcast at 300 feet above ground level... visibility 3 miles in mist

chain.label: Regulations allow descent below MDA on approach lights alone, where obstacle clearance is not assured
chain.trigger: the current Federal Aviation Regulations that allow pilots to descend below the MDA into a region in which safe obstacle clearance is not assured based upon seeing only the airport approach lights

chain.label: Sterile cockpit rule violated; unprofessional banter continued below 10,000 feet
chain.trigger: the pilots' conversation after the airplane descended below 10,000 feet msl... was not consistent with these sterile cockpit procedures

chain.label: Division of duties abandoned and standard callouts omitted; first officer did not challenge the captain
chain.trigger: their failure to adhere to the established division of duties between the flying and nonflying (monitoring) pilot

caused_by.evidence: reflected a demeanor and cockpit environment that fostered deviation from established standard procedures, CRM disciplines, division of duties, and professionalism
his failure to monitor and react to the captain's deviations from nonprecision approach procedures was consistent with the degrading effects (slowed reactions and/or tunnel vision) of fatigue

chain.label: Captain continued the 1,200 fpm descent below the MDA without the required visual cues
chain.trigger: their descent below the minimum descent altitude (MDA) before required visual cues were available (which continued unmoderated until the airplane struck the trees)

caused_by.evidence: the captain should have leveled off and focused on the flight instruments and the first officer should have instructed him to level off

these regulations can have the unintended effect of encouraging some pilots to descend below the MDA in an attempt to acquire visual cues that will permit them to continue the approach, as occurred in this case
Consistent with the degrading effects of fatigue, the captain made a risky decision to continue the approach based on inadequate visual cues
the low ceiling and reduced visibility at IRK made the nonprecision approach more challenging

chain.label: Pilots fixated on the approach lights and misjudged sink rate and height above terrain
chain.trigger: the captain's failure to stop or slow the airplane's descent indicates that he was not aware of the airplane's excessive descent rate and/or significantly misjudged its proximity to the ground

caused_by.evidence: both pilots were largely preoccupied with looking for the approach lights
With only an approach light or lights for approach path reference, a pilot could focus on those lights while flying into the ground
the pilots failed to follow established procedures to effectively monitor the airplane's descent rate and height above terrain during the later stages of the approach

chain.label: Airplane descended into treetops on a ridge short of the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane first contacted the trees more than 1.3 nautical mile (nm) south of the approach end of runway 36, about 50 feet agl

caused_by.evidence: the accident airplane initially impacted trees about 996 feet msl, which was about 62 feet below the '100 feet above TDZE' altitude
the first officer exclaimed, 'trees,' and the captain stated, 'no, stop'

chain.label: Collision with trees along the approach path
chain.trigger: The first sounds of impact with the trees were recorded at 1936:55.2

caused_by.evidence: a swath of broken trees continued in a northerly direction to the main wreckage area

chain.label: Crash 1.2 nm short of runway 36; airplane destroyed by impact and postimpact fire
chain.trigger: The airplane was destroyed by impact and a postimpact fire.

caused_by.evidence: The main wreckage site was located about 775 feet north of the initial impact site

chain.label: 13 occupants fatally injured, 2 seriously injured
chain.trigger: The captain, first officer, and 11 of the 13 passengers were fatally injured, and 2 passengers received serious injuries.

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for all fatally injured airplane occupants was determined to be multiple blunt force injuries experienced during the impact sequence
